## Background

Today we are going to learn all about the **ggplot2** package into R.

There are tons of graphic packages in R. These include "base R graphics" (like the `plot()` function we used last day) and add on packages like **ggplot2**

### Comparing base graphics with ggplot

we can use the in-build data frame `cars` to play with plotting:


```{r}
head (cars)
```

```{r}
plot(cars)
```
now with ggplot:
First I need to install the package with 
`install.packages()`
> I do not want to run `install.packages("ggplot")` in my quarto document as this will result me in reinstalling the package everytime i render my report.

Every time I want to use function from a given package I need to load it up with a `library()` call: 

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cars)
```

Every ggplot needs at least 3 things:

- the **data** (data.frame we want to plot from)
- the **aesthetics** (how the columns of the data map to the plot)
- the **geom** (how you want the plot drawn, points, lines, etc.)

```{r}
ggplot(data=cars) +
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) + 
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method="lm", se=F) +
  theme_bw() + 
  labs(x="Speed in (MPH)", 
       y= "Stopping Distance (ft)", 
       title= "Silly Plot of Stopping Distances")
```

## Gene Expression Plot 

Read the data from online: 

```{r}
url <- "https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt"
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)
```

```{r}
ggplot(genes) + 
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2,) +
geom_point()
```


> Q. How many genes are in this dataset? 

```{r}
nrow(genes)
```


> Q. How many are "up" regulated? 

```{r}
table(genes$State)
```
```{r}
sum (genes$State == "up" )
```

> Q. what percentage of genes are "down" regulated ? 

```{r}
72 / 5196 * 100
```

```{r}
n.total <- nrow(genes)
n.down <- sum(genes$State == "down")

round( n.down/n.total *100, 4)
```

```{r}
myplot <- ggplot(genes) + 
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2,col=State) +
  geom_point() +  
  scale_colour_manual( values=c("magenta","pink","purple") ) + 
  labs(x= "Control (no drug)", 
       y= "drug treated", 
       title = "Gene expression changes upon drug treatment", 
       subtitle= "GLP-1 inhibator from Novo") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
myplot
```

We can Install extra packages with `install.packages()` like theme packages 
for spongebob colors or any actual useful one like **patchwork** for combining plots: 

```{r}
library(patchwork)

# Setup some example plots 
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(mpg, disp))
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_boxplot(aes(gear, disp, group = gear))
p3 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_smooth(aes(disp, qsec))
p4 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_bar(aes(carb))

# Use patchwork to combine them here:
(p1 | p2 | p3 ) /
  p4
```

```{r}
myplot + 
  facet_wrap(~State)
```

## The GapMinder data

The gapminder is rather a famous and has lots of stuff we can plot ;-)

```{r}
# File location online
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"

gapminder <- read.delim(url)
```

Have a wee peak
```{r}
head (gapminder)
```


> Q. How many data enteries are there in this dataset ? 

```{r}
nrow(gapminder)
```


> Q. How many countries are in this dataset?

```{r}
length(unique (gapminder$country) )
```

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(gdpPercap,lifeExp, col=continent) +
  geom_point()  
```

Break out a facet wrap to distinguish each contitent 

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) + 
  aes(gdpPercap,lifeExp, col=continent) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~continent)
```

Histograms of 
```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp,fill=continent) +
  geom_histogram()
```

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp,fill=continent) +
  geom_boxplot()
```
